checked.comment: The setting matches the paper: a finite arm set D that spans R^d, ||x||<=1, ||theta_t||<=1, a non-oblivious (adaptive) adversary and zero noise, so losses lie in [-1,1]. The algorithm uses d, T and |D|.

This is the corrupted stochastic setting with fixed theta, an arbitrary corruption c_t that may depend on history, and C = sum|c_t|. Regret is measured on the corrupted losses, and the paper assumes a unique optimal arm. The paper only says the noise is 'zero-mean', but Lemma 6 uses ell_t(x_t)^2 <= 1, which implicitly supports bounded_pm1.
Registry id ftrl_linear_negentropy_g_optimal matches FTRL with a negative-entropy regulariser and G-optimal design exploration.
The adversarial bound O(sqrt(dT ln T ln(|D|T))) from Theorem thm:thmregret is recorded correctly, with K=|D|. The learning rate uses ln T, so the horizon is known.
The corrupted-stochastic bound O(d ln T ln(|D|T)/Delta_min + sqrt(C d ln T ln(|D|T)/Delta_min)) is recorded correctly.

summary: The extraction is accurate and needs no corrections. It records both bounds of the single main theorem (adversarial and corrupted stochastic) with the right expressions, symbol mapping (K=|D|), quantity and horizon. The settings, algorithm registry id and cited results from Table 1 and the concurrent-work comparison all match the source. The self-bounding and regret-decomposition lemmas are technical and were correctly left out.
